```python
def simplify(x, n):
    
    a, b = x.split("/")
    c, d = n.split("/")
    numerator = int(a) * int(c)
    denom = int(b) * int(d)
    if (numerator/denom == int(numerator/denom)):
        return True
    return False

# Unit test for function simplify
def test_simplify():
    # Product is exactly 1
    assert simplify("1/2", "2/1") == True
    assert simplify("1/3", "3/1") == True
    assert simplify("2/8", "4/1") == True   # 8/8 = 1

    # Product is a whole number greater than 1
    assert simplify("7/2", "2/1") == True   # 14/2 = 7
    assert simplify("5/1", "1/1") == True   # 5
    assert simplify("3/9", "9/3") == True   # 27/27 = 3
    assert simplify("1/7", "14/2") == True  # 14/14 = 1

    # Product is not a whole number
    assert simplify("1/2", "3/1") == False  # 3/2
    assert simplify("1/4", "2/3") == False  # 2/12
    assert simplify("1/5", "1/5") == False  # 1/25
    assert simplify("2/3", "3/5") == False  # 6/15

    # Numerator zero -> product is 0, a whole number
    assert simplify("0/1", "5/2") == True
    assert simplify("0/3", "1/3") == True

    # Negative fractions
    assert simplify("-1/2", "2/1") == True   # -2/2 = -1
    assert simplify("-1/2", "3/1") == False  # -3/2
    assert simplify("-2/4", "-4/2") == True  # 8/8 = 1

    # Whole number inputs
    assert simplify("1/1", "1/1") == True
    assert simplify("10/1", "1/10") == True

    print("All test_simplify tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_simplify()
```
